items.stem: A finance lead wants daily cost totals in USD for each team workspace. The script must use credentials that the usage and cost endpoints accept. Which setup meets the constraint?
options: Call the usage and cost endpoints with the workspace API key that the script already holds.
Set the Cost API bucket to one minute to get finer daily totals.
Stream each response usage field into a warehouse, and rebuild the totals every hour.
Call the usage and cost endpoints with an Admin API key, and read the daily cost report by workspace.
items.rationale: The usage and cost endpoints accept Admin API credentials only, so a workspace key fails. The Cost report gives daily totals in USD, and it can group them by workspace.
items.trap: A workspace API key looks sufficient for a script, but the usage and cost endpoints do not accept workspace keys.

items.stem: An on-call engineer must see a traffic spike within seconds. The team has a usage report and a cost report. The team cannot wait for a daily total. Which action meets the constraint?
options: Poll the Usage and Cost API once per minute and alert on each new total.
Set a monthly spend alert on the workspace to catch a spike within seconds.
Read the usage fields in each live response, and log them as responses return.
Add a live response log, and also run a weekly cost review with finance.
items.rationale: The aggregate reports typically lag each request by up to 5 minutes, so they are too slow for this check. Per-response usage fields report each call as it completes.
items.trap: Polling the usage endpoints every minute looks fast, but the aggregate data can trail each request by up to 5 minutes.

items.stem: A company runs one workspace for each team. The owner wants a monthly budget for each team and rate limits for each model. Select two settings that meet both requests.
options: Set a monthly spend limit and alerts on each team workspace.
Set a per-minute spend limit on each workspace to cap traffic bursts.
Set rate limits per model on requests, input tokens, and output tokens per minute.
Put every team on the Default Workspace, and set one spend limit there.
items.rationale: A spend limit and its alerts apply to one workspace, so each team gets its own budget. Rate limits cap requests and tokens per minute for each model.
items.trap: One spend limit on the Default Workspace looks like a shared budget, but that workspace accepts no spend limit.
